messages:
zoe (CS): FYI Brightline reported a sharp drop in embeddings throughput at 2026-03-28 09:15 UTC. Tokens/sec looks normal, vectors/sec down ~60%. Customer saw timeouts and 429s. Request IDs: r_qk3a, r_qk3b. Attaching a minimal repro curl they ran.

support-bot: Got it — creating incident alert #INC-1024 and paging oncall.

raj (SE): thanks — can you paste the exact curl payload + headers and which model/variant they're calling? also: are they batching client-side or sending single-item requests?

zoe (CS): payload (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' \
  -H 'X-Client-Id: brightline-prod' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1","input":["doc1","doc2","doc3"],"top_k":0}'
```
They say they send 32 small requests/sec (each ~3 inputs). No streaming. They rotated a service-account billing key yesterday afternoon.

mike (ML): odd — tokens/sec fine but vectors/sec down suggests post-model path slowdown (batching/aggregation or kvcache/batching config). Can we get GPU metrics for the serving pool for those request IDs? queue depth, avg batch size, GPU util, and any kvcache churn.

lee (SRE): pulling metrics now. quick snapshot (avg during window):
```
pool: embed-prod-us-east-2
gpu_util_avg: 26%
queue_depth_peak: 142
avg_batch_size: 1.3
kvcache_evictions_per_min: 3.8k
tokens_per_sec: 192000
vectors_per_sec: 72000
sched_wait_ms_p95: 120
nvlink_errors: 0
```
Looks like a lot of tiny batches queued with long scheduler wait. GPU not saturated but scheduling/packing poor.

raj (SE): tokens/sec / vectors/sec ratio here is ~2.67 which is unexpected given input lengths. Two hypotheses: (1) client dimensionality mismatch causing us to fall back to a slower compatibility path, or (2) routing to a variant that lacks optimized kernels so we get poor vectorization. Can you repro locally with a controlled batch (single request with 128 inputs) and run with verbose logging? Also include the model routing header `X-Model-Variant` if present.

zoe (CS): repro run - single request 128 inputs. Response times: 200ms per request but vectors/sec still low ~30k. Pasting server-side snippet from logs around r_qk3a: 
```
[2026-03-28T09:15:12Z] request_id=r_qk3a routing=redwood-embed-1 -> redwood-embed-1-compat
[info] batch_window_ms=4 avg_batch_size=1.2 fallback=compat-path
[warning] kvcache: evict_count=4200 reason=memory_pressure
[error] compat_path: kernel_selection=scalar_fallback
```

mike (ML): that log is telling: route fell back to `-compat` variant and is using scalar/compat kernels. That would explain low throughput despite low GPU util. Why did routing pick compat? Check model metadata and kernel availability. Maybe the rotated billing/service key changed model artifact metadata or version indexing in catalog so the optimized variant wasn't marked as compatible.

lee (SRE): running model route lookup: 
```
$ /srv/bin/model-route lookup redwood-embed-1 --pool embed-prod-us-east-2
primary: redwood-embed-1@v12 (optimized)
fallback: redwood-embed-1-compat@v7 (compat path)
route_decision: variant pinned -> redwood-embed-1-compat (reason=missing_kernel_metadata)
metadata_error: model_v12/metadata.json: access denied (403)
```
Aha — model metadata file access returned 403 during routing. Timestamp correlates with the service-account key rotation.

raj (SE): so routing couldn't read kernel metadata and defaulted to compat variant. Compat variant uses scalar kernels and small-batch behavior -> tiny avg batch sizes -> high scheduling overhead -> vectors/sec collapse. This matches observed symptoms.

mike (ML): mitigation: (1) temporarily pin customers to the known-optimized variant `redwood-embed-1@v12` at the routing layer, (2) increase `batch_window_ms` to 8 for this pool to improve packing, and (3) enable prefix pinning to preserve kvcache during the fix. Commands: 
```
# pin route for brightline-prod
/routing/bin/pin --client brightline-prod --model redwood-embed-1 --variant redwood-embed-1@v12
# bump batching policy
/infra/bin/policy set embed-prod-us-east-2 batch_window_ms=8
# enable prefix pinning
/infra/bin/kvconfig set embed-prod-us-east-2 pin_prefixes=true
```

zoe (CS): applied pin + batch_window bump. Re-ran customer repro. Immediate improvement: vectors/sec up to 124k, avg_batch_size -> 12, sched_wait_p95 -> 36ms. Customer reports no more 429s. :thumbsup:

lee (SRE): creating follow-up infra ticket to audit service-account rotation path and ensure model metadata read permissions are part of key rotation playbook. I've linked incident INC-1024 -> TICKET-2087.

raj (SE): action items:
- raj: add permission-check step to key-rotation runbook (TICKET-2087)
- lee: add alert if model metadata reads return 403 during routing
- mike: add a regression test that asserts optimized variant is reachable after key rotations
- zoe: confirm with customer and close incident once they validate 24h stability

mike (ML): nice find everyone. I'll follow up with a small PR to make routing log clearer when metadata reads fail (include credential id).

zoe (CS): customer confirmed 1h later they're green. Closing incident after 24h watch. Thanks all.
